job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: Rohan and his sister Meera were helping their father fix a string of decorative lights for Diwali. Meera noticed that when they added more bulbs in parallel, the brightness remained steady. She asked if the battery would run out faster if they added more branches. Their father explained that the battery does not supply a fixed current; instead, the current depends on the total resistance of the circuit. He showed them that adding more resistors in parallel actually decreases the total resistance, allowing more current to flow from the source. Rohan then picked up a copper wire and wondered if it had any resistance at all. His father clarified that even excellent conductors like copper possess some resistance, which is why wires can heat up when a large current passes through them. He also reminded them that current is not consumed by the bulbs; the same amount of charge that enters a bulb must exit it. Finally, he pointed out that while electrons drift slowly, the electric field that pushes them travels through the circuit almost instantly, ensuring all bulbs light up the moment the switch is closed.
response.summary: This story explains how parallel circuits function, the nature of resistance in conductors, and the behavior of electric current. It clarifies that current is not consumed by components and that electric fields propagate rapidly.
